figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage USD 5.15/h (27-4-202(a)). Tipped cash wage not less than USD 2.13/h from 2001-04-01, employer makes up to 5.15; tipped employee = customarily more than USD 30/month in tips; monthly tip record on IRS forms (b). Youth under 20 may be paid USD 4.25/h for the first 90 consecutive days, no displacement (c). Excluded from 'employee': agriculture; domestic service in a private home; bona fide executive/administrative/professional; US, state and political-subdivision employees; voluntary or non-employment nonprofit service; outside salesmen paid commission only; on-call ambulance drivers (27-4-201(a)(iv)). Records (name, address, occupation, rate, amount per pay period, hours per day and week) kept 2 years (27-4-203). No indexation; no local minimum wage. FLSA USD 7.25 binds FLSA-covered employers.

instrument_name: W.S. 27-4-101, 27-4-104, 27-4-501(a)(iii), 27-4-507 Wage payment, final pay, vacation, tips
figure_or_rule_carried: Semimonthly paydays (by the 1st for wages to the 15th of the prior month; by the 15th for the rest) only for railroads, mines, refineries, oil and gas, factories, mills and workshops; preceding working day if the payday is not a working day; law posted in 2 places (27-4-101(a)). Direct deposit only if voluntarily authorised by the employee (b). Agricultural operations exempt (c). Laid-off or suspended employees paid on the next regular payday (d). Final pay on quit or discharge: no later than the employer's usual regular payday (or CBA time); employer may offset sums the employee owes; commission sales agents with custody of accounts excluded; 18% p.a. interest plus attorney fees on suit (27-4-104). Wages include fringe benefits; accrued vacation is wages (payable at termination) unless a written forfeiture policy is acknowledged in writing by the employee (27-4-501(a)(iii)). DWS wage claims capped at 2 months' wages outside bankruptcy (27-4-502(a)). Tips are the employee's sole property (27-4-507(a)). Wage assignments for loans under 200 USD need written employer acceptance and filing; a married employee needs the spouse's written consent (27-4-110/111). No deduction for dishonoured checks except listed cases (27-4-116).

instrument_name: W.S. 27-3-102(a)(xviii) definition of wage for UI contributions (taxable wage base and exclusions); 27-3-303(a) statewide average annual wage
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base = 55% of the statewide average annual wage (27-3-303(a): total wages in the calendar year preceding June 1 / 12-month average employment) rounded to the lowest 100 USD, per employee per employer or predecessor per calendar year, INCLUDING wages under any other state UI law. Excluded from wage (to the extent not FUTA wages): retirement/sickness/medical/death plan premiums; employer-paid FICA; non-obligatory dismissal pay; tips not reportable under 3306(s); convenience meals/lodging on premises; sick pay after 6 months of illness; sec. 125 benefits excluding cash; wages of a deceased worker paid after the year of death; sec. 129 dependent care; educational assistance; achievement awards; sec. 120 legal services; group-term life cost; moving expenses; employer contributions to qualified plans/IRA and 403(b); SUB payments; workers' compensation benefits. 8% of the average annual wage rounded to the lowest 50 USD = monetary eligibility (27-3-306(d)(i)).

instrument_name: W.S. 27-3-105, 27-3-107, 27-3-108 UI coverage: government, nonprofit, religious, agricultural, domestic, excluded services
figure_or_rule_carried: Covered: state and political-subdivision service incl. appointed officials (105(a)(i)); 3306(c)(8) nonprofits with 4+ individuals in 20 weeks (a)(ii); Indian tribes (a)(iii). Not covered: churches and church-controlled organisations, ordained ministers, religious-order members, elected officials, legislature/judiciary members, national guard, temporary emergency government hires (105(b)). Agricultural labor covered at 20,000 USD cash wages in a quarter or 10+ workers in 20 weeks (107(c)); H-2A workers exempt while FUTA exempts them (107(h)). Domestic service covered at 1,000 USD cash wages in a quarter (107(g)). Excluded: service for a spouse or child, under-21 child for a parent (108(a)(i)); federal service; under-18 newspaper carriers/direct sellers; licensed real-estate agents; students employed by their school and spouses in financial-aid programmes; certified co-op students; hospital patients; booth-rent barbers/stylists; leased owner-operators with contract; casual labor (under 50 USD, outside the course of business); LLC members unless the LLC elects (108(a)(xiii)).

instrument_name: W.S. 27-6-107 to 27-6-114 child labor; 27-5-101 state/county employee overtime
figure_or_rule_carried: No employment under 14 except farm, domestic, lawn/yard; proof of age on file for under 16; under 16: at most 8 hours in 12, not before 5 a.m. or after 10 p.m. before a school day (midnight otherwise), not during school hours if enrolled. The overtime statute covers only state and county employees (8 h/day, 40 h/week, 1.5x if authorised by the governing body, 27-5-101); no private-sector state overtime rule: FLSA governs.

instrument_name: W.S. 27-1-115 State directory of new hires
figure_or_rule_carried: Report to DWS within 20 days of hire (electronic filers: two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart): employee name, address, SSN, first date of services for remuneration; employer name, address and FEIN. On the IRS W-4 or a DWS-approved equivalent; mail, electronic or magnetic. Multistate electronic filers may elect one state under federal law (c).

instrument_name: W.S. 27-14-202 Workers' compensation payroll reports and premiums (Wyoming state fund)
figure_or_rule_carried: The employer forwards the certified payroll of extrahazardous employees with the premium monthly, due the last day of the month after the month earnings are paid; quarterly reporting by permission (due the last day of the month after quarter end); consolidated-account election; DWS joint payroll reporting system with UI (g). Premium is employer-paid (27-14-201 rates); no employee-share provision located in chapter 14.

instrument_name: Wyoming DWS Office of the Director memo to the Joint Labor, Health and Social Services Committee, with attachments (LSO interim meeting 2025-10-16)
article_or_section: pp. 5-6 'UI Tax Rates and CARES Act Funding'; p. 4 eligibility
figure_or_rule_carried: UI tax paid solely by the employer; rate = base rate (benefit ratio over 3 fiscal years, or the industry average for under 3 years) + fund balance factor (positive below 3.5% of payroll, negative above 4%) + noncharge/ineffective-charge factor. Minimum rate 0% in 2022-2024; 2025 minimum 0.14% (= 45.36 USD per employee at the 32,400 base, re-derived); statutory maximum 10% (8.5% base + 1.5% factor cap, re-derived from 27-3-503(b)/505); 2025: 13,066 employers at 0.14%, 396 at 10%. 8% of the statewide average annual wage 'for 2025' = 4,900 USD. 2026 minimum/maximum rates NOT in this document.

instrument_name: Wyoming DWS Wyoming-specific labor law posters (Drive PDF linked from the DWS Labor Law Poster page, last updated June 2025)
article_or_section: p.3 State Minimum Wage; p.4 UI; p.7 WC; p.8 non-compete
figure_or_rule_carried: Wyoming state minimum wage 5.15 USD/h; training wage 4.25 USD/h under age 20 for the first 90 days (second document family confirming 27-4-202). UI taxes paid by employers. WC required for extra-hazardous industries, optional otherwise. Non-compete ban effective 2025-07-01, W.S. 1-23-108 (not payroll).

instrument_name: W.S. 1-15-501 to 1-15-511 Continuing garnishment; 1-11-401 jurors (Title 1 compiled)
figure_or_rule_carried: Continuing-garnishment lien lasts until the earliest of termination, satisfaction, dismissal or 90 days after service; one writ at a time in order of service; a child-support IWO (20-6-201..222) has priority and tolls the writ (1-15-504(c)). Limit = lesser of 25% of weekly disposable earnings or the excess over 30x the federal minimum hourly wage (same as CCPA; 1-15-511). Earnings include pension/deferred compensation, exclude per diem. No discharge for garnishment (1-15-509). Jury service: no discharge or threat; no paid jury-leave duty (1-11-401).

instrument_name: W.S. 20-6-201 to 20-6-222 Income withholding for support (Title 20 compiled)
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding starts no later than the first pay period after service; remit to the state disbursement unit within 7 days after the obligor is paid, with name, SSN and withholding date; employer fee 5 USD per payment, retained from remaining income; support + fee capped at 15 U.S.C. 1673; termination notice to the clerk within 30 days (last address, new payor); health-coverage lapse notice within 30 days; IWO has priority over any other state-law process; the uniform federal IWO form is accepted (20-6-210(c)).

instrument_name: W.S. 40-12-501 and 40-12-502 Computer security breach notification (Title 40 compiled)
figure_or_rule_carried: Breach notice to affected Wyoming residents for personal identifying information (name + elements in W.S. 6-3-901(b)(iii)-(xiv), incl. SSN, unless redacted to no more than 5 digits). No pay-statement SSN-truncation rule found in Titles 27 or 40 (keyword scans).

instrument_name: W.S. 22-2-111 Employees time off to vote (Title 22 compiled)
figure_or_rule_carried: 1 hour of paid time off (other than meal hours, at the employer's convenience) on primary, general or special congressional election day, no loss of pay if the employee votes; not applicable with 3+ consecutive nonworking hours while polls are open.

figure_or_rule_carried: Labor Standards handles wage claims for work physically done within Wyoming; out-of-state work and older claims go to US DOL WHD; state wage claims generally within 2 years of the due date. Landing page: enforces wage claims, youth employment, prevailing wage and Wyoming labor preference, resident contractor certificates.

instrument_name: W.S. 27-3-502 Determination of employer and employment; service suppliers and temporary service contractors
figure_or_rule_carried: Service supplier (27-3-501(a)(viii)) pays contributions on wages it pays to workers serving a client; if not a service supplier or the client pays directly, the client is the employing unit; supplier keeps separate records, submits a quarterly list of all clients and separate quarterly reports for each client; client jointly and severally liable for unpaid contributions; temporary service contractor is the employing unit of its temporary workers.
